title: The cloud worker's model is a hardcoded constant — make it configurable, and default it to a model that converges
description:
Measured on run_215b7cbff9dd405c80d738be45cccde5 (2026-08-22), the first cloud run whose substrate worked end to end. Three real ticks, 90-minute budget each, workers on deepseek-v4-flash:

  201  exit 124 at the bound, 0 work commits — did not converge
  5jo  exit 0, real correct work (e0898b00)
  5qj  exit 124 at the bound, 0 commits, 4 paths salvaged — did not converge

One of three. These are not toy ticks (201 is scrolling in a bubbletea TUI, 5qj is a workerd lifecycle problem in vitest) and flash ground through 90 minutes of 94-99%-cached calls without finishing two of them. That is a model-capability result, not a substrate one — everything around it worked.

Tick y45 predicted exactly this shape and already did the work: flash at implement.balanced/economy, deepseek-v4-pro at implement.strong (63% vs 53% on DeepSWE v1.1). Both are Workers AI, so both stay on the Cloudflare credit — the operator's constraint that Phase 2 uses only Workers AI models is unaffected either way.

TWO THINGS TO FIX, and the second is the one that lasts:

1. WORKER_DEFAULT_MODEL in cloud/factory/src/worker-boot.ts is a hardcoded constant (tick ys3 put it there, correctly, to get the worker off the repository's [roles.implement]). There is no way to change it without editing source and redeploying. Give the deployment a variable for it, the way RUN_MODEL/the budgets already work, so the worker model is an operator decision rather than a source edit.

2. Change the DEFAULT to deepseek-v4-pro on the evidence above. Say plainly in the same change what it costs: y45 measured pro at roughly 2.4x flash per task, and pro delivered about half its post-warm cache opportunities against flash's 23/23 — so the real multiple on a long agentic run is worse than the headline. A flash worker that does not converge costs 100% of its tokens for 0% of the work, which is the comparison that actually matters.

DO NOT collapse this into 'always use the expensive model'. The right end state is per-tick tier selection (a small tick gets flash, a hard one gets pro), which is what the [roles.implement].tiers table already expresses for local workers and what the cloud path has no plumbing for yet. If that is more than this tick, implement the variable plus the new default and say precisely what per-tier selection would need — that is a good Phase 3 candidate.
